# windows_disk (Resource)

Adopts a physical disk on a remote Windows host via SSH and PowerShell (`Get-Disk` / `Set-Disk` / `Initialize-Disk`) and manages its online/offline state, read-only flag and — for uninitialized (`RAW`) disks only — its partition style.

The resource never creates or destroys disk hardware: Create resolves exactly one of `unique_id`, `serial_number`, `location` or `number` to a single disk (zero matches is an error, several matches are an `ambiguous_disk` error) and records the stable `unique_id` as the Terraform ID; Delete only drops the adoption from state and makes no remote call, so the disk and its data are left untouched.

Disks hosting the OS (`is_boot` / `is_system`), the active pagefile, the crash-dump target, or clustered disks are refused fail-closed with `protected_storage`, as is a disk whose placement cannot be determined. Prefer the `unique_id` selector: disk `number` values are assigned by Windows at scan time and can shift across reboots or when disks are added or removed (using `number` emits a warning).

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    windows = {
      source  = "kfrlabs/windows"
      version = "~> 0.1"
    }
  }
}

provider "windows" {
  host     = var.windows_host
  username = var.windows_username
  password = var.windows_password
}

# Minimal example: adopt a data disk by its stable UniqueId and keep it
# online and writable. The resource never creates or destroys disk hardware:
# applying adopts the matching disk (its UniqueId becomes the Terraform ID)
# and destroying only drops the adoption from state.
resource "windows_disk" "data" {
  unique_id = "SCSI\\DISK&VEN_MSFT&PROD_VIRTUAL_DISK&REV_1.0"
}

# Advanced example: adopt an uninitialized (RAW) disk by serial number,
# initialize it to GPT and take it offline (e.g. a disk reserved for a
# cluster or a backup rotation). Only a RAW disk is initialized in place:
# adopting an already-initialized disk with a different style is a
# partition_style_mismatch error.
resource "windows_disk" "reserved" {
  serial_number   = "6000c296-abc123"
  partition_style = "GPT"
  is_offline      = true
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `is_offline` (Boolean) Whether the disk is offline (`Set-Disk -IsOffline`). Null (unset) leaves the observed state unmanaged; otherwise the flag is enforced in place.
- `is_read_only` (Boolean) Whether the disk is read-only (`Set-Disk -IsReadOnly`). Null (unset) leaves the observed state unmanaged; otherwise the flag is enforced in place.
- `location` (String) Get-Disk Location (adapter path) of the disk to adopt, matched case-insensitively after trimming whitespace. Exactly one of unique_id, serial_number, location and number must be set. ForceNew.
- `number` (Number) Get-Disk Number of the disk to adopt. Exactly one of unique_id, serial_number, location and number must be set. ForceNew. Disk numbers are assigned by Windows at scan time and can shift across reboots or when disks are added or removed: using number emits a warning, prefer unique_id.
- `partition_style` (String) Desired partition style for uninitialized (RAW) disks: GPT or MBR. Only a RAW disk is initialized in place; adopting an already-initialized disk with a different style is a partition_style_mismatch error (converting GPT<->MBR destroys data and is out of scope). Unset leaves the style unmanaged. ForceNew.
- `serial_number` (String) Get-Disk SerialNumber of the disk to adopt, matched case-insensitively after trimming whitespace. Exactly one of unique_id, serial_number, location and number must be set. ForceNew.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `unique_id` (String) Stable Get-Disk UniqueId of the disk to adopt (e.g. `SCSI\DISK&VEN_...`). Exactly one of unique_id, serial_number, location and number must be set. ForceNew. This is the Terraform ID; prefer it over number.

### Read-Only

- `bus_type` (String) Get-Disk BusType (e.g. SATA, NVMe, RAID, USB, Virtual), as observed on the host.
- `friendly_name` (String) Get-Disk FriendlyName, as observed on the host.
- `health_status` (String) Get-Disk HealthStatus (e.g. Healthy), as observed on the host.
- `id` (String) Resource identifier; the stable Get-Disk UniqueId of the adopted disk.
- `is_boot` (Boolean) Whether the disk is the boot disk, as observed on the host. Boot disks are refused with protected_storage.
- `is_clustered` (Boolean) Whether the disk is clustered, as observed on the host. Clustered disks are refused with protected_storage.
- `is_system` (Boolean) Whether the disk is the system disk, as observed on the host. System disks are refused with protected_storage.
- `operational_status` (String) Get-Disk OperationalStatus (e.g. Online, Offline), as observed on the host.
- `size_bytes` (Number) Get-Disk Size in bytes, as observed on the host.

### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an existing disk by its stable Get-Disk UniqueId.
terraform import windows_disk.data 'SCSI\DISK&VEN_MSFT&PROD_VIRTUAL_DISK&REV_1.0'
```
